title: field-operator-readiness-and-sla-evidence-playbook-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
This playbook describes a field-operator-centric on-call and incident response program focused on readiness, evidence collection for SLA/regulatory requests, and repeatable game-day rehearsals. It is intended for SREs, service owners, and first-responders who operate Redwood inference runtime services.

Scope
- Applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API routes, dedicated pools, private control plane bridges).
- Covers incidents that cause SLO degradations (latency, availability, correctness) or require customer comms.
- This document does not replace service-specific runbooks; it supplements them with readiness and evidence templates.

Goals
1. Ensure responders can stabilize incidents within 10 minutes for P1 latency regressions and 60 minutes for regional outages (see SLO thresholds).
2. Provide a standardized evidence package (timeline, metrics, snapshots, logs) for SLA calculations and regulatory audits within 48 hours.
3. Make game-day rehearsals repeatable with measurable skills and a triage scoring rubric.

Definitions
- Field Operator: primary on-call engineer responsible for first-response actions and evidence capture.
- Bridge Operator: person who manages the cross-team incident bridge and external comms.
- SLO: Service Level Objective; see SLO table below.

SLOs and Thresholds (reference)
| Service | SLO (p99) | Alert threshold | Escalation window |
| Hosted inference (text-gen) | 200 ms | p99 > 250 ms for 5m | escalate at 10m |
| Embedding service | 75 ms | p99 > 120 ms for 5m | escalate at 10m |
| Dedicated pool ingress | 99.95% availability | error rate > 0.5% for 5m | escalate immediately |

Incident lifecycle (quick flow)
1) Detect: automated alerts (Prometheus/Alertmanager), synthetic failures, or customer reports.
2) Acknowledge: primary field operator acknowledges in pager system within 2 minutes.
3) Triage & Contain: collect immediate evidence, apply containment playbook.
4) Bridge & Notify: if customer-impacting or SLO breach possible, stand up bridge and inform stakeholders.
5) Remediate: apply antidote (config rollback, capacity add, model-fallback).
6) Recover: restore service and monitor for regression.
7) Close & Evidence: produce formal SLA evidence bundle and postmortem.

Roles & responsibilities
- Field Operator (primary): initial triage, evidence capture, execute runbook steps, own followups.
- Backup Operator (secondary): take over if primary is overloaded/unavailable; review evidence.
- Bridge Operator: run bridge template, coordinate stakeholders, publish status updates.
- Service Owner: approve long-term remediation and drive postmortem actions.
- Customer Success (when required): own customer-facing explanations and credits.

Contact matrix (example)
- Pager -> Field Operator on-call (Team: Serving-runtime-pager)
- Escalation 1 -> On-call tech lead (text message + Slack)
- Escalation 2 -> SRE Duty Manager -> Exec notification if incident > 2 hours

On-call rotation & handoff checklist
Every handoff should include the 5-minute continuity checklist below before transfer of duty: 
- Confirm local runbook state (document any in-progress mitigations).
- Share outstanding alerts and current incident timelines (timestamps + brief cause hypotheses).
- Verify metric dashboards (p50/p95/p99, error rates, queue lengths).
- Confirm access to key systems (SSH bastion, GCP/AZURE console, KMS access token).
- Update escalation contact list if any changes.

Handoff template (copy into Slack on shift start)
1. On-call name: <name>
2. Current incidents: none / <short list>
3. Known degradations: none / <short list>
4. Active maintenance windows: <times>

Game-day rehearsal program
Purpose: validate operator readiness and evidence workflows under controlled stress.
Cadence: quarterly for serving teams; monthly for high-risk services (new model rollouts, major latency-sensitive routes).
Game-day roles: facilitator, primary operator, secondary operator, bridge operator, observer(s), customer-voice actor.
Scenario design principles:
- Start with a reproducible trigger (synthetic load generator, KV cache flush, model weight swap).
- Include at least one cross-system dependency failure (e.g., metrics ingestion or storage outage).
- Exercise customer comms and SLA evidence packaging.

Scoring rubric (0-5 per skill)
- Detection & acknowledgement (0-5)
- Triage quality (evidence, hypothesis) (0-5)
- Runbook execution accuracy (0-5)
- Bridge & comms clarity (0-5)
- Remediation completeness (0-5)

Runbook templates (field operator)
Use this as the canonical step sequence for latency spike P1s. Copy into service-specific runbooks and customize variables.
1) Confirm alert: record alert ID, time, and primary metric snapshot.
2) Collect evidence (do not rotate logs yet):
   - Screenshot of p99, p95 graphs.
   - tail -n 500 /var/log/serving/runtime.log | grep "ERROR" --context=3 > /tmp/incident-errors.log
   - curl -sS https://admin.internal/metrics?service=<svc>&range=5m > /tmp/metrics.json
3) Check KV cache health and hit-rate: redis-cli -h redis.svc info keyspace
4) Apply containment (example):
   - Reduce request concurrency on route: curl -X POST https://ops.internal/config -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","concurrency":20}'
   - If feature-flagged can fallback to smaller model: opsctl model fallback --service <svc> --to small-v1
5) If no improvement within 10 minutes, escalate to tech lead and stand up bridge.

SLA evidence package checklist (deliver within 48h)
- Incident chronicle (timeline with ISO timestamps)
- Alert and pager logs (export from PagerDuty/Oncall tool)
- Metric snapshots (CSV/JSON p50/p95/p99 time series for impacted windows)
- Configuration diffs (git commit SHAs and applied infra changes)
- Logs and traces (trace IDs, span excerpts)
- Model and deployment artifacts (model SHA, image tag)
- Customer impact statement (estimated degraded requests, tenant list)

Evidence export commands (examples)
- Pager export: pagerctl export --incident <id> --format json > /tmp/pager.json
- Metrics: promql_export --query "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))" --output /tmp/p99.csv
- Traces: jaeger-cli fetch --service serving-runtime --start "2026-01-10T10:00:00Z" --end "2026-01-10T10:10:00Z" --output traces.zip

Postmortem template (one-page summary required within 72h)
- Title: "<brief incident summary>"
- Severity: P1/P2/P3
- Impact: affected routes, customer list, estimated degraded QPS
- Detection time / Recovery time / Total downtime or SLO delta
- Root cause statement (1-2 sentences)
- Contributing factors (bulleted)
- Immediate remediation taken (bulleted)
- Long-term fixes (owner, ETA)
- SLA evidence bundle link (attach ZIP or internal storage link)
- Lessons learned & blocking items for follow-up

Customer status templates (for Bridge Operator)
1) Initial acknowledgement (within 30 minutes)
Subject: Redwood Inference — Incident acknowledged for <service>
Body: We are aware of an issue impacting <brief impact>. Our on-call team is investigating and we will provide an update within 30 minutes. Incident ID: <id>.

2) Status update (every 30–60 minutes while active)
Subject: Update: Incident <id> — <current summary>
Body: Current status: (investigating/mitigating/monitoring). Impact: <what customers see>. Next update: <eta>.

3) Post-incident closure
Subject: Resolved: Incident <id> — <summary and root cause>
Body: Incident resolved at <time>. Root cause: <summary>. Mitigation applied: <what we did>. If you experienced degraded requests, we will follow up with account team for any credits.

Status page short messages (examples)
- Investigation: "We are investigating increased latency on the /v1/generate route. Some requests may be slower than usual."
- Mitigating: "Mitigation in progress: traffic diverted to fallback model while we restore capacity."
- Resolved: "Issue resolved. Full service restored and we are monitoring for regressions."

Retention and evidence storage policy
- SLA evidence packages are stored in the secure incident-bucket for 90 days for internal audits.
- For enterprise customers with special retention, export to their compliance bucket and notify Security.

Training & onboarding for new field operators
- Week 0: shadowing a live on-call with an assigned mentor.
- Week 1: complete two runbook micro-exercises and one supervised game-day scenario.
- Quarterly: mandatory game-day cadence and skill review.

Appendix A — Quick-check commands and snippets
- Check service health: curl -sS https://admin.internal/health/<svc> | jq .status
- Restart worker process: kubectl -n serving rollout restart deployment/<svc>-worker
- Snapshot p99: promql_export --query "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[10m])) by (le))" --output /tmp/p99_snapshot.csv

Appendix B — Links
- Service runbook index: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-index
- Pager playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-command-playbook-and-escalation-matrix-2024
- Evidence storage location: gs://incidents-evidence/internal/

Notes and governance
- This playbook is the canonical readiness and evidence process; service owners must adopt it and add service-specific parameters.
- Changes to SLO thresholds or the evidence retention policy require SRE manager approval.

Revision history
- 2025-10-12: Created by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-12-05: Added SLA evidence checklist and export commands (reviewed by Marcus Chen).
- 2026-02-03: Updated SLO thresholds and game-day cadence (approved).
